The multiplier is ε = 0.1. Each edit's displacement is capped at ε times the local nearest-neighbor radius rᵢ (‖x̃ᵢ − xᵢ‖₂ ≤ ε · rᵢ), and this single value is used across all 39 NLP settings and all 80 CelebA settings without per-setting tuning.

The general model's Bloom-target separability peaks at Layer 28 (the coder model's peaks later, at Layer 36). The methodology identifies the general model as a Qwen3-Next model, with the name given as "Qwen3-Next-80BA3B-Instruct" (as it appears in the passage, with the hyphen in "80B-A3B" apparently lost in extraction); the passage is cut off right after that name, so I can't confirm the exact full designation beyond that.

ALS dominates the corpus, accounting for 78.1% of the 3.43 hours (2.51 h), versus 16.1% for PD and 5.8% for stroke. The corpus is used only for ASR evaluation because of its variability, not its modest size: it spans three pathologies, several intelligibility levels, and heterogeneous acoustic conditions, so any training split would be too skewed per stratum for reliable adaptation.

(One caveat: the passages don't state that the corpus is Spanish, but the ALS dominance and the rationale for evaluation-only use are stated directly.)
High-quality data is OpenMathInstruct2 (0.8B unique tokens), low-quality data is FineWeb, and evaluation is on MATH500, reporting accuracy against cumulative HQ tokens.

The cutoff is δ = 0.3. A conflict is counted at turn τ when a slot value is overwritten and the cosine similarity between the user utterance embedding and the embedding of the prior-value probe phrase (e.g., "The {slot} is {old_value}") falls below 0.3.

Artifact components are identified by their correlation with reference signals (e.g., EOG for ocular and ECG for cardiac artifacts). For each artifact type p, a component is flagged as nuisance if the absolute Pearson correlation between its time-series and the reference series φp meets or exceeds a chosen threshold τp, i.e., Sp = {i : |ρ(ŝi, φp)| ≥ τp}. These flagged components are then projected back to sensor space and subtracted from the raw recording to give the cleaned signal.

The oracle baseline was evaluated in the task allocation domain on the "most representative models," which the passage identifies as GLM-4.7, GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-5.1, and DeepSeek-V3.2. The oracle outperformed the centralized baseline significantly for GLM-4.7 and GPT-4.1-mini, with smaller gaps for GPT-5.1 and DeepSeek-V3.2.

Without meta features on a new set, DraftEncoder only matches the linear model without meta features, and it falls short of the heuristic baseline (which implicitly has meta statistics for the full expansion). It is, however, competitive with the linear model that has meta features.

List-type questions are scored with the mean F1-score (the official BioASQ measure, computed from precision and recall against the gold list). The pipeline's best list F-measure rose substantially, from 0.2734 in Batch 1 to 0.5652 in Batch 4, which the authors attribute to the addition and refinement of the collaborative list-answer pipeline.

A response counts as a confirmed success only if both judges (GPT-4o and DeepSeek-chat) simultaneously score it ≥4 on the 1–5 rubric (where 5 is full compliance, and forensically framed content counts as harmful if actionable). Under this criterion, RetroCoT raised GPT-4o's attack success rate from 0% for the direct request to 58% on AdvBench (n=50).

Spatial coordinates (x, y) are encoded with Multi-resolution Hash Encoding (MHE), which is used to capture high-frequency anatomical details. This is part of the decoupled hybrid design, in which the spectral offset Δω is handled separately by the physics-informed Lorentz Encoding, and the two feature sets are concatenated before the MLP.

On X-shaped and Two-moons, the expert left out is RBIG: two experts dominate and RBIG has a near-zero share (Neff ≈ 2.17 and 2.09). On the real regression targets (BLR, BPR, Weibull), the suppressed expert is instead RealNVP, leaving a two-way MAF/RBIG split (Neff ≈ 1.99–2.00).

Prevailing neural TPP objectives are local: they decompose into a sum of per-event losses, each comparing one event to the ground truth conditional on the preceding events. SIGTPP instead optimises a single global, sequence-level loss (Sig-W): the l2 distance between the expected truncated signatures of the embedded generated paths and the embedded data paths. The data signature is precomputed once, and gradients flow back through the generator, so global properties like autocorrelation and long-range dependencies receive direct loss signal.

The passage says Ragas's non-LLM metrics compare retrieved spans to reference spans using Levenshtein distance, which gives a relevant value only when the compared spans are of similar size. Here the spans differ greatly in size, so the correlation with recall is very weak. (The passage doesn't mention the telecom dataset or human ratings, but the explanation itself is stated in the text.)

The pipeline uses DialogueSidon, a diffusion-based model that jointly performs speech separation and restoration (denoising, dereverberation, etc.) on degraded in-the-wild dialogue mixtures. It maps each monaural two-speaker clip to a pair of speaker-wise waveforms, which are stored as stereo audio with one speaker per channel.

The speech encoder's default chunk size C is 100 frames. When the chunk size is reduced to 1, resynthesis intelligibility is impaired, which the paper attributes to inaccurate syllable segmentation (see Table 3), even though that setting has a higher bitrate.

The paper says programmatic generators produce valid variants faster and at lower cost than LLM-based generation, which enables scalable, heterogeneous corpus expansion under a shared reporting format. In the data-transformation experiments, a combinatorial search over 6,000 pipelines found a single-transform RandomPosterize configuration reaching 61.24% accuracy, outperforming the best LLM-generated pipeline, which reached 57.28%.

The Lyapunov projection acts directly on the hidden state, enforcing the safe energy set after the quantised write-back. The threshold Vmax is estimated from the initial token energy distribution on the training set: it is set as γ times a p-quantile of the initial energies V(h⁰ᵢ) of the training samples.

Per the passage, SelfMem's framework supplies the human-designed procedural principles, the available memory tools, the feedback channels, and the audit constraints (while also keeping the raw transcript as an immutable source of truth). The agent determines the concrete memory strategy itself: which transcript turns or snippets to inspect, what to store, what to compress or update, what to preserve exactly, and what to leave recoverable from the original transcript.

The EIG reward is scaled by 1/ln(2), which yields a normalized scalar r_EIG(ξt, Θt) in the [0, 1] range. (The passage doesn't name the method "ASIG" explicitly, but this describes the EIG reward scaling in the 20 Questions setup.)

Morphological segmentation comes right before the multi-step script disambiguation: a whitespace split is followed by dictionary-guided merging of stems and suffixes, producing morphologically coherent segments. The disambiguation itself has three steps: vowel harmony recovery, Latin-assisted normalization, and Cyrillic normalization, which together turn the underspecified Traditional script into a phonologically specified Cyrillic representation.

Freezing old ranks cut average forgetting from 0.0631 (task-wise elbow) to 0.0283, while raising the final average score from 0.8095 to 0.8178 (the forward-preserving variant reached 0.8193 with 0.0340 forgetting). As for why freezing inside one shared adapter is considered unreliable, the paper says only that hard freezing reduces plasticity, soft freezing lets old ranks drift, and parameter-space anchoring does not preserve old-task outputs, so ReCoLoRA-TaskBank instead gives each task its own isolated adapter branch.

The strongest strategy discovered during SelfMem's refinement search reached a held-out BEAM score of 0.510. For comparison, the default no-refinement strategy scored 0.472, and the final agent-synthesized strategy scored 0.497.

Unlike Sprint, Sparse-Reslim does not replace skipped tokens with learnable mask embeddings, and it does not need an extra linear projection to fuse them back. Instead, the unselected tokens receive zero delta, so they keep their actual pre-routing (dense-early) representations exactly, forming an implicit identity skip connection. Only the residual delta from the sparse middle blocks is scattered additively, with no added parameters, back to the selected token positions.
Each fine-tuning run (including evaluations) was done on a single NVIDIA L4 GPU and took roughly 12–16 hours.

ASIG uses an Expected Information Gain (EIG) reward in its multi-turn extension of Group Relative Policy Optimisation. On the 14B model, it improved the 20 Questions success rate over the baseline by 4.2 percentage points on the animals category (and 1.8 points on plants).

Per the passage, the standard bridge plug-in is optimized by the cavity law, not the denoiser. The context does not mention an "Oracle Distance" analysis by name, but it states this result directly for the paper's treatment of discrete diffusion.

On MHEALTH, RepMixer (B2) did not beat full self-attention (B1): attention was marginally ahead by 0.32 F1 points. On USC-HAD the result inverted, with RepMixer outperforming self-attention by 1.72 F1 points, which the paper attributes to USC-HAD's longer 500-sample sequences, where early-stage attention's quadratic cost brings less benefit than the convolutional inductive bias suits single-IMU signals.

In the hybrid ablation pipeline, a dedicated RoBERTa-Base encoder trained for regression predicted the continuous valence/arousal scores for the extracted text spans, overriding the decoder model's numerical outputs. The paper reports that the generative LLM "performed exceptionally well" on the quadruplet prediction task, which the authors found surprising since encoders are usually considered more stable for regression. The passages don't give specific quadruplet-task scores, and they don't name the team as "The Classics."

SIGTPP underperforms on the CRPS by approximately 6.5% compared to VAE and DDPM. The authors suggest this is because optimising a path-level distributional objective favours global distributional alignment, without necessarily improving conditional calibration relative to methods trained directly with conditional losses.

118 of the 120 HallusionBench abstentions produced no reasoning chain at all, even at the 1,024-token budget. (Of the 231 originally-unclear samples rerun at an extended budget, 119 remained unresolved.)

According to the passages, TANS trains contrastively on encoded model weights and dataset characteristics, but it uses alignment only as a learned similarity proxy to retrieve known nearest-neighbour models, leaving the underlying latent space largely unchanged. WeightCLIP instead aims to make the contrastive alignment itself shape a shared, dataset-aligned weight-space representation, so that a dataset can act as a reference frame for retrieval, prompting, interpolation, optimization, and decoding into full models. The passages don't give WeightCLIP's specific architecture or training details beyond this goal.

The empirical Stein tensor combines sampling noise with a deterministic multiscale low-rank bias (the population tensor is itself a structured multi-spike object, rather than a single spike as in standard tensor PCA). While the first-order spiked approximation suffices for efficient recovery via spectral tensor unfolding, the fine-grained Edgeworth expansion is crucial for the analysis of SGD (Section 6).

The passage identifies these as AusElectricity and ETTh2. On both, the crossing is non-monotonic: classical methods beat the zero-shot foundation model with only 2% of training data, but the foundation model regains the lead at 100% training data. (By contrast, FRED-MD, Saugeen, Solar-10min and Traffic stay classical-favored through 100%.)

The passage doesn't name the specific foundation models or classical methods compared (Chronos, Moirai, Lag-Llama, XGBoost, ETS, ARIMA), only "the best foundation model" versus "the best classical method," so I can't confirm those particular models from this text.

The paper reports that it tested and abandoned the Library of Congress Subject Headings, the FAST faceted vocabulary, and Roget-style thesauri. None of them matched the precision of the inductively emerged ontology that fits this kind of memorial corpus.

The passages say FGAA outperformed "both traditional CAA" on Gemma-2 models, though the text is cut off before naming the second baseline. CAA (Contrastive Activation Addition) computes its steering vector as the average difference in activations at a specific layer l between positive and negative examples of a behavior: v_t = (1/N) Σ (a_l(x+_i) − a_l(x−_i)), averaged over a set of contrasting pairs (e.g., truthful answers vs. hallucinations).

By default, BiSCo-LLM targets seven linear module categories: q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj (the attention projections), and gate_proj, up_proj, and down_proj (the MLP projections). Partial settings, such as compressing only down_proj or only the attention projections, are also evaluated.

In the pressure experiments, HRRR data from 2017–2019 is used for training and 2020 for evaluation, with December excluded because of a known issue affecting this variable between December 2020 and July 2022. (For the other experiments, 2017–2024 is used with 2022 reserved for evaluation to compare against the Aurora base model.)

The global λ is dropped: the per-sample local-radius-capped λi (Eq. 6) eliminates it from the proposed method. The remaining step-controlling hyperparameters are not tuned per setting; they are fixed to the same values (e.g., ε = 0.1, H = 60, λmax = 64, kmin = 8) across all 119 settings (39 NLP × 80 CelebA).

TR-RAG's only extra cost over standard RL is a single teacher forward pass on student-visited prefixes (no teacher rollouts are needed). The cited 2024 method on credit assignment in RL training of LLMs is VinePPO ("VinePPO: Refining credit assignment in RL training of LLMs," Kazemnejad et al.). However, the passages don't state that TR-RAG links this problem to noisy sequence-level rewards, so I can't confirm that part of the framing from the context given.

GPT-4o-mini. The specialist for the highest training charge (q = 16e) was fine-tuned on only the AIMD frames at that charge, which per Table 4 is 968 frames (all at the sparse 14.8 Å setting, with no 13.8 Å dense frames).

HARVEY does not rely on unlearning (as ABL does) or on backdoor suppression (as CBD does); instead it prevents backdoor injection by removing poisonous samples through dataset splitting. And unlike DBD and D-ST, it does not use a fixed splitting ratio when partitioning the data: it splits the dataset adaptively, which helps preserve natural accuracy.

The custom SGA (alignment) head does not keep linear-time scaling. Although Jamba-1.5-Mini was chosen for the linear O(N) scaling of its Mamba layers, the SGA head computes full cross-sequence similarity matrices (M_micro ∈ R^{La×Lc}), which reintroduces an O(La × Lc) quadratic compute and memory bottleneck at the end of the pipeline. The passage doesn't name the system "IVD-SSM" explicitly, but this matches the head and backbone it describes.

The clinical validated events ratio R is the sum of occurrence counts c(fj; D) over the clinically validated tokens (the set Fc), divided by the sum of counts over all tokens F. This measures how much of the surrogate's token importance falls on tokens that match known clinical predictors. For LOS, the reference set consists of patient diagnoses and comorbidities (ICD-10-CM codes), Hospital Frailty Risk Score diagnostic codes (109 specific ICD-10 codes from current and past 2 years of records), and physiological measurements (heart rate, blood pressure, temperature, oxygen saturation) including those in the National Early Warning Score (LOINC/SNOMED codes).

The refinement optimizes the task loss through the decoder while constraining the latents to a hyperspherical shell and to a local neighborhood. This keeps the adjusted latents within the aligned latent space during test-time adaptation.

MINDE-C is the variant that does not consistently break: the passage says MINDE-J consistently breaks across all synthetic copula experiments, while MINDE-C only fails on the high-dimensional embedding experiments (Table 8b).

According to the passage, swapping the composition structure barely moves the grok-rate at the n = 2000 budget on the 10^4 domain, whereas raising M from 8 to 10 collapses it. (The passage doesn't mention a model called "Glimmer-1-Base"; it describes the task and setup only.)
Each round trains the reference model on the subset S(i) for Tpoi = 10 epochs, and the LGA loss uses γ = 0.01 (chosen to avoid overfitting to the few benign samples in the subset).

Switching the monitor from GPT-5 mini to GPT-5 nano raises the odds of undetected attack success by a factor of 52.9 at a 5% false-positive rate. The paper cautions that this is partly because GPT-5 nano is a deliberately weak monitor, so the figure reflects the gap between a clearly weak and a capable trusted monitor rather than a precise constant. (The passage doesn't name the "FakeLab" study explicitly, but this is the monitor comparison it reports.)

The losing sample x_l is synthesized from the student sampler's own output by applying a degradation operator G (e.g., a low-pass filter) to it, with a stop-gradient: x_l = G(sg[x_φ]). This uses the student's output as the baseline rather than an external target.

FUSE is benchmarked against two simulation-based inference baselines: NPE (Neural Posterior Estimation) and FMPE (Flow Matching Posterior Estimation). All estimators are trained on the same budget of simulated orbits, and a long-run Parallel Tempered MCMC (PTMCMC) chain serves as the reference posterior.

At R = 128 (178M models), IsoLoCo's loss is about 9.7% higher than the AdamW DP baseline (vs. DiLoCo's 16.5%). The combined IsoLoCo + MuLoCo approach improves on IsoLoCo with an AdamW inner optimizer by 0.92% at R = 128, which is the endpoint of a gain that grows from 0.60% at R = 32.

The experiments were run at a single model scale of 100M parameters. The limitations section notes the study evaluates one domain (math), one model scale (100M), one HQ budget (0.8B tokens), and one LQ source (FineWeb).

The passage groups interactive theorem provers into four categories: (1) Dependent Type Theory systems such as Lean and Coq, (2) First-Order Logic systems such as ACL2 (with first-order ATPs like Vampire and E-prover often integrated via hammer-style frameworks), (3) Higher-Order Logic systems such as Isabelle/HOL, which emphasize automation through tools like sledgehammer, and (4) Hybrid Systems such as PVS, which bridges HOL and dependent types through predicate subtyping.

InfoBridge learns its drift functions vA and vB via conditional bridge matching. The two stochastic processes, QA and QB, start from the joint distribution and from the product of marginals respectively, and the estimator's error depends solely on how accurate the learned drifts are. (The passage describes this from Kholkin et al., 2025 and does not detail further specifics of the training procedure, such as architectures or hyperparameters.)
With the dense potential, there are 0 dead all-fail updates per seed, compared with roughly 16 of 40 iterations under outcome-only training (Figure 9, right).

The voice-converted utterance is never used as the training target; it only serves as the source of the per-word reference clips spliced into the prompt. The target is always the codec of the original waveform (cu,tgt = Enc(au)), so GRAFT's output quality is not limited by the quality of the voice conversion model.
Numina-LeanAgent employs a general-purpose coding agent that uses the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to interact with Lean autonomously, and it does not require task-specific training.

According to the paper's limitations section, the worst-case MASE under full fine-tuning at low fractions (≤5%) exceeded 23 and came from Moirai-S on the Solar-10min dataset. The paper reports 109 catastrophic failures (MASE > 10) in this regime and recommends LoRA as the default instead.

Quantizing the language backbone to INT4 (cfg1) raised Qwen3-VL's energy consumption on the Jetson Orin NX by 54.7% (from 12.31 J to 19.04 J), per Table 8. The authors attribute this to the extra time spent on BitsAndBytes dequantization operations, which increases power usage despite the lower VRAM footprint.
The reference model unlearns for only one epoch per round. This is done to avoid learning divergence and to help the model stably unlearn the benign samples.

I can only speak to what the passage says, and it doesn't mention a "mutinfo suite" or copula-theoretic benchmarking work specifically. What it does say is that naïve pdf-based MI estimation is biased because the separately modeled joint and marginal densities are generally inconsistent with each other: the true marginals of the estimated joint π̂(x, y) typically don't match the separately estimated π̂(x) and π̂(y) (e.g., π̂(x) ≠ ∫π̂(x, y)dy). Gaussian mixtures are cited as a generative model that inherently yields correct pointwise MI, since their marginals are analytically consistent with the joint, though vanilla Gaussian KDE doesn't scale to complex, high-dimensional data.

Under AdamW at 350M parameters (~1B tokens), CLER-DeltaNet (scalar) ended with a validation loss of 3.4258 versus 3.4068 for the DeltaNet baseline, i.e., a worse result by +0.0190. The paper attributes the lack of benefit to a basis (space) mismatch: the delta-rule residual is a local correction tied to one layer's memory state, keys, value target, and feature map, so when routed into another layer's independently learned value space it need not be aligned and competes with the receiver's own write target.

In the λ-interpolation sweep, the sigmoid midpoint of the collapse falls near CKA ≈ 0.85, with the channel fully closing below roughly CKA ≈ 0.70. The passage doesn't state that this CKA is specifically "linear" CKA, only that it's computed on h2 activations using 10,000 MNIST test images.

The retrieval corpus contains 5,358 chunks. These were produced by converting the 687 UK Government public health guidance documents to markdown and splitting them by markdown header levels, with the full header hierarchy appended to each chunk for context.

The context describes four criteria used by the rubric-based judge (GPT-OSS-120B): factual consistency, completeness, clarity, and faithfulness to official guidance. The averaged teacher target for position i only uses future steps in Ti, i.e., steps t > k at which i is still masked. Steps at which i has already been decoded (committed) are excluded, because there the model would simply read back the committed token rather than genuinely predict it, so those steps carry no real predictive signal.
The pair with the longest path length is C→W (System UI), at 137.0. By contrast, B→8 has the shortest path length at 27.7, so path length varies by nearly a factor of five across the ten pairs.

Presupposition turned out to be the load-bearing component: presupposition alone reached 5%, A+C (presupposition plus backward CoT) reached 15%, and presupposition with the forensic persona reached 50%, whereas persona + backward CoT without presupposition got 0%. The underlying phenomenon, presupposition accommodation, describes the tendency of cooperative language agents to silently accept unstated background assumptions in order to make an utterance coherent, so the model accepts the presupposed harmful outcome as given and shifts from evaluating whether to comply to analyzing how it happened.

The passage says the frontend uses a pre-trained IndicWav2Vec model, extracting features from layers 7–11 and projecting them to 80 dimensions (with the upstream model parameters kept frozen). The unknown second derivatives of the true weights and bias, d²W/dt² and d²b/dt², are approximated in practice using centered difference quotients of the discrete (computed) weight and bias values. These feed the interpolation estimates that give ωw_n and ωb_n.

To obtain the "true" error for comparison with the upper bound, the authors assume that the exact loss J̃({x_s(t_T)}) ≈ 0, i.e., that there exists a true network that both fits the training data well and generalizes well, achieving near-zero validation loss. The true error is then estimated by treating this loss as zero, leaving J̃ of the discrete solution as the error.

Combining the disagreement-preserving sign (s = −1) with the joint L_F1 + L_CE objective produced the largest calibration improvement, a cross-entropy change of ΔCE = −0.0993 (alongside a modest F1 gain of ΔF1 = +0.0043). In CLVR, each routing-capable layer's projection Pl is zero-initialized. As a result, the routed contribution (εl,t = Pl vl,t) starts at exactly zero, so at the start of training the routed signal adds nothing to the shared residual stream and only grows as Pl is learned.

Applying Gaussian sketching to one partitioned subset (the θ̂ᵢ estimator) takes O(mdn/k) time, whereas sketching the whole data set (the β̂ᵢ estimator) takes O(mdn). So sketching a subset is k times cheaper, and for large n and small d the whole-data approach can even be slower than standard OLS (O(nd²)), while the subset approach stays efficient for large k.

The improvement appeared only with the true Schwartz continuum. Both a random permutation of the value geometry and an empirical co-occurrence graph failed to produce the theory-aware coherence gains when used with the same decoder.

Per the context, for CNNs and ResNets the state at stage l can be defined as a pooled feature representation, hl = GAP(Fl(x)), where Fl(x) is the stage's feature map and GAP is global average pooling. The hidden-state dimension then equals the number of channels at each stage, so state-order reduction amounts to channel-width reduction.

Expert-panel framing raises HRR from 66.5% (no-source) to 79.4%, a +12.9 percentage-point increment (odds ratio 2.40). HRR is defined as P(a1 ≠ t | a0 = t): the probability that a model's answer after the cue differs from the correct answer t, given that its answer before the cue was correct.
